stem: What does B2B stand for?

options.content: Business to business
Bank to bank

options.content: Browser to browser software

options.content: B2C

stem: What is the difference between e-business and e-commerce?

options.content: They mean exactly the same thing
E-commerce covers only the paying of staff and the keeping of the accounts of a business
options.rationale: E-commerce is about buying and selling.

options.content: E-business needs no internet at all
E-commerce is the buying and selling part of e-business, which covers all business activities done electronically

explanation: E-commerce is one part of e-business.

stem: Which is a benefit of e-commerce to a small business?

options.content: It removes the need for any delivery
options.rationale: Goods still have to be delivered.

stem: A seller receives a message that says a customer has paid by mobile money, but she has not received a confirmation from the mobile money service. What should she do?

options.content: Send the goods at once, because the message says that the customer has paid
options.rationale: The message may be a fake.

options.content: Ask the customer to send the PIN
Wait until the payment is confirmed by the service before sending the goods
Delete the order and the customer's details
options.rationale: This does not solve the problem.

explanation: Always check a payment with the payment service.
hints: Where should the proof of payment come from?

stem: In a business, which of these is a fixed cost?

options.content: The cloth used for each item made
options.rationale: Materials change with the number of items.

options.content: Delivery paid for each item sold
options.rationale: Delivery changes with the number of items.

options.content: Monthly rent for a work space
options.rationale: Correct: it does not change with the number of items sold.

options.content: A commission paid on each sale

explanation: Fixed costs stay the same whatever the number of units sold.
hints: Does the cost change if more units are sold?

stem: A business has a profit on paper for the month but runs out of money to pay its supplier. What is the most likely cause?

options.content: Revenue is always equal to cash flow
Fixed costs are always zero
Break-even has been reached, so cash can never run out of money in the business
options.rationale: Reaching break-even does not guarantee cash.

options.content: Customers bought on credit and have not yet paid, so cash has not come in
options.rationale: Correct: profit and cash flow are different.

explanation: Profit is not the same as cash.

stem: Which advice is best for a small online seller who is worried about fraud?

options.content: Accept screenshots of payments as proof
Confirm payments through the payment service, use secure checkout and never ask for PINs or card numbers in chat
Ask customers to send their card details and PINs by message so that payments can be checked
options.rationale: This puts their data at risk.

options.content: Only sell to people who ask politely

explanation: Verify payments with the service and keep details safe.
hints: Where does reliable proof of payment come from?

stem: A business that has reached its break-even point makes neither a profit nor a loss.
explanation: True. At break-even, revenue equals total costs.

stem: A mobile money agent charges 2% of the amount sent. A customer sends US\$45 to a supplier. Calculate the fee, in US dollars.
Describe the e-commerce models B2C and B2B, with an example of each. [3]

points.description: B2C: a business sells to individual consumers
B2B: a business sells to other businesses
An example of each, such as an online clothes shop (B2C) and a supplier of computer parts to repair shops (B2B)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: B2C is when a business sells to individual consumers, for example an online clothes shop. B2B is when a business sells to other businesses, for example a supplier of computer parts to repair shops.

hints: Name the model and describe who sells to whom.

stem: Explain two benefits and two risks of e-commerce for a small business. [4]

points.description: Benefit: a wider market, because customers in other towns can be reached
Benefit: lower costs, because no expensive shop or large staff is needed
Risk: fraud or fake payments, so payments must be checked
Risk: dependence on the internet, mobile network and electricity, or problems with delivery

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It gives a wider market because customers in other towns can be reached, and it lowers costs because no expensive shop or large staff is needed. The risks are fraud or fake payments, and dependence on the internet, mobile network and electricity or problems with delivery.

hints: Two benefits and two risks, each linked to a small business.

stem: Compare mobile money and card payments for a small online shop in Zimbabwe. [4]

points.description: Mobile money needs no bank account and is widely used by customers
Mobile money may charge fees and needs the network to be working
Card payments suit customers who have bank accounts and give a secure online checkout through a gateway
Fewer customers have cards, and the seller must use a secure gateway and trust it

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Mobile money needs no bank account and is widely used, but fees may apply and the network must be working. Card payments suit customers with bank accounts and use a secure gateway, but fewer customers have cards.

hints: Mobile money, cards, bank transfer, cash on delivery.

stem: Explain why a business can make a profit in a month and still have a cash problem. [4]

points.description: Profit is revenue minus costs, counting sales even if customers have not yet paid
Cash flow records only the money that has actually come in and gone out
Customers who pay late mean that cash comes in later than the sale
Stock bought in advance or bills that are due early take cash out before it comes in, so cash can run out

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Profit counts sales even if customers have not paid, while cash flow records only the money that has come in and gone out. If customers pay late, or stock and bills must be paid before the sales money arrives, the business can run out of cash although it makes a profit.

hints: Explain how cash flow can differ from profit.

stem: A web designer in Bulawayo sells a website template for US\$20. Each template costs US\$12 to customise and send. Her fixed costs are US\$640 a month.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the contribution from selling one template, in US dollars.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the break-even number of templates sold in a month.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit when 110 templates are sold in a month.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Suggest three ways in which she could lower her break-even point.

points.description: Increase the price of a template (if customers will still buy)
Lower the variable cost of each template, for example by using ready-made parts
Lower the fixed costs, for example by working from home or choosing a cheaper internet plan

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Increase the price if customers will still buy, lower the variable cost of each template, and lower the fixed costs, for example by working from home.

stem:
A small online shop starts April with US\$560 in cash. Its cash in and cash out for three months are shown.

| Month | Opening cash | Cash in | Cash out | Closing cash |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| April | US\$560 | US\$900 | US\$720 | ? |
| May | US\$740 | US\$650 | US\$810 | ? |
| June | US\$580 | US\$1100 | US\$950 | ? |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the closing cash for April, in US dollars.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the closing cash for May, in US dollars.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the closing cash for June, in US dollars.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Cash fell during May. Suggest three actions the owner could take to improve cash flow.

points.description: Ask customers for part or full payment before the goods are sent
Delay or reduce spending on stock and other costs that are not urgent
Negotiate longer payment terms with suppliers or keep a cash reserve

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Ask customers to pay before the goods are sent, delay or reduce spending that is not urgent, and negotiate longer payment terms with suppliers.

explanation: Closing cash is US\$740 in April, US\$580 in May and US\$730 in June.
hints: Closing cash = opening cash + cash in − cash out.
